definition: The Radiant AI is a technology developed by Bethesda Softworks for The Elder Scrolls video games.
details: It allows non-player characters (NPCs) to make choices and engage in behaviors more complex than in past titles. The technology was developed for The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion and expanded in The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim; it is also used in Fallout 3, Fallout: New Vegas and Fallout 4, also published by Bethesda, with 3 and 4 being developed by them as well. Radiant AI was not present in Bethesda's most recent title, Starfield. In February 2026, Todd Howard said that while artificial intelligence is "certainly not a fad," Bethesda is "being incredibly cautious" and does not use it for creative generation, such as writing quests or producing art, for upcoming titles including The Elder Scrolls VI.

explainer.lead: Radiant AI is technology developed by Bethesda Softworks that lets non-player characters in its games make choices and behave more complexly than in earlier titles. It matters as an early, prominent example of AI-driven NPC behavior in major games.

tiers.eli5: It is the system that lets characters in a game decide what to do on their own instead of just following a fixed script.
tiers.practitioner: Game developers use it to give NPCs richer, less scripted behavior within a game world. A pitfall is that it was absent from Bethesda's Starfield, showing not every title carries the system forward.
tiers.paperLevel: Described as technology allowing NPCs to make choices and engage in behaviors more complex than in past titles; no formal definition or bound is given.

explainer.example: In The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion, NPCs driven by Radiant AI make choices rather than only following fixed behavior.
